title: Implement reconcile_status_scalars helper
description: Add a pure helper `reconcile_status_scalars(original: &str, focus: &Focus) -> String` to `src/brain/emit.rs`. It should locate the YAML frontmatter (between the first two `---` lines) and replace or append the `now`, `next`, and `blocked` keys. The value for each scalar should be a double-quoted string joining the blocks in that queue (e.g., `"repo:id — title, repo2:id2 — title2"`), or the literal `[]` if the queue is empty. Add unit tests in `tests/brain_emit.rs` (or inline if applicable) to verify replacement, addition, and preservation of surrounding content.

title: Implement plan_status_frontmatter planner
description: Add `plan_status_frontmatter(files: &[(StateSource, StateFile)], graph: &StateGraph, config: &BrainConfig) -> EmitPlan` to `src/brain/emit.rs`. For each state file, use `derived_focus_for` (for project kind) or `derive_brain_focus` (for brain kind) to get its focus. Resolve its `status.md` path (use `status_file` from `brain.toml` via `config`, or fallback to sibling `status.md`). If the file exists, read its content, apply `reconcile_status_scalars`, and if the output differs, emit an `EmitAction` to overwrite the file. Add integration tests for this planner in `tests/brain_emit.rs`.

title: Wire plan_status_frontmatter into emit_state
description: In `src/lib.rs`, wire the new `plan_status_frontmatter` planner into the `emit_state` driver so it executes alongside `plan_state_json`, `plan_master_plan_tables`, etc. Apply the resulting plan via `apply_plan(&plan, write)`.
